bihar_raw_news.title: "Election where people can rein in existing system with their votes": Prashant Kishor on ...
bihar_raw_news.content: "Election where people can rein in existing system with their votes": Prashant Kishor on Bihar MLC polls ANI | Updated: Oct 21, 2026 19:32 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Muzaffarpur (Bihar) [India], October 19 (ANI): Jan Suraaj Party founder and MLA Prashant Kishor said on Wednesday that the upcoming Bihar MLC elections will not change the state government or opposition leadership, emphasising that in these elections people can rein in the existing system in Bihar with their votes. Addressing reporters in Muzaffarpur , Kishor emphasised that the exercise will not alter the leadership status quo in the state, noting that the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government remains firmly in place and Tejashwi Yadav will continue as the Leader of the Opposition. "This is not an election to form a government. The government is the NDA's and will remain so. This is not an election to remove anyone from the government. Tejashwi Yadav is the Leader of the Opposition and will remain so, but this is an election where people can rein in the existing system in Bihar with their votes," Prashant Kishor told reporters. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced biennial elections to the Legislative Councils in Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. The elections will be held for seats in the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies following the completion of the terms of the sitting members. According to the Commission, the terms of eight members in Bihar, four in Karnataka, five in Maharashtra and 11 in Uttar Pradesh are ending, resulting in vacancies in the respective constituencies. The Model Code of Conduct has come into force with immediate effect in the constituencies concerned. The four Graduates' constituencies include Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut, and Kosi, and four Teachers' constituencies include Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut, and Saran. The tenures of the sitting members of eight constituencies will expire on November 16. According to the Election Commission, the formal notification for the elections was issued on September 29, 2026. The last date for filing nominations was October 6, followed by scrutiny of nominations on October 7. Candidates will be able to withdraw their nominations until October 9. Polling for the respective Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies in all four states will be held on October 23 from 8 am to 4 pm. The counting of votes is scheduled for October 27, and the entire election process will be completed by October 31. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Begins NSS Survey on Household Finances - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Begins NSS Survey on Household Finances 21 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Bihar, has commenced fieldwork under the 81st round of the National Sample Survey (NSS) to assess household income, expenditure, assets, investments and outstanding debt across rural and urban areas. The survey, scheduled to continue until June 2027, will generate data on agricultural households’ income and household debt and investment patterns to support evidence-based policymaking. Key Points The exercise focuses on assessing the economic condition of agricultural households and examining household debt and investment, through: Agricultural Household Survey: It will collect information on income from farming, horticulture, animal husbandry and other sources. All-India Debt and Investment Survey: It will assess household assets, investments and outstanding loans from banks, moneylenders and other sources. National Sample Survey Established in 1950 , the National Sample Survey (NSS) is a multi-subject, continuous sample survey programme designed to collect data on various aspects of India’s economy and society for use by Central and State government agencies. Initially focused on rural areas and data required for national accounts, its coverage gradually expanded to include rural and urban India and a wide range of socio-economic issues. Its surveys broadly cover household socio-economic conditions, landholdings, livestock and agriculture , industrial establishments and enterprises, and village-level information. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's GI-Tagged Mithila Makhana Expands Global Reach, Exports Cross 7000 Tonnes
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar’s GI-Tagged Mithila Makhana Expands Global Reach, Exports Cross 7,000 Tonnes IBEF October 21, 2026 India exported more than 7,000 metric tonnes of makhana and value-added makhana products to over 20 international markets in FY26, according to the Ministry of Commerce. These markets include the United States, the Middle East and Africa, reflecting the product’s expanding global reach. Bihar accounts for nearly 85% of India’s makhana production, making it the country’s leading producer. Mithila Makhana, which has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, is gaining international recognition for its nutritional benefits and versatility. Growing health awareness, startups developing value-added products and the participation of Farmer-Producer Organisations (FPOs) are helping expand the sector beyond its traditional markets. India is the world’s largest producer of makhana, with cultivation concentrated mainly in Bihar, West Bengal and Assam. The Government of India has introduced measures to strengthen the sector and support exports. A separate Harmonised System (HS) code for makhana came into effect in July 2025, enabling its distinct classification in international trade. The National Makhana Board, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, was formally launched in Bihar on September 15, 2025. In addition, the government approved the Central Sector Scheme for the Development of Makhana, with an outlay of Rs. 476.03 crore (US$ 53.87 million) for 2025-26 to 2030-31. The scheme focuses on research and innovation, quality seed availability, farmer training, improved harvesting and post-harvest practices, value addition, branding, marketing, exports and quality control. Allocations of Rs. 30 crore (US$ 3.39 million) for FY26 and Rs. 90 crore (US$ 9.47 million) for FY27 have been approved under the scheme. These initiatives aim to modernise makhana cultivation and processing, strengthen farmers’ incomes and expand the global market for Bihar’s GI-tagged Mithila Makhana. bihar_raw_news.content: Home · Interview Gujarat’s technology ecosystem is driving innovation, digital transformation and economic growth. As Gujarat strengthens its position in semiconductors, biotechnology, digital governance and emerging technologies, the Department of Science & Technology is driving the State’s innovation agenda. Smt. Ponugumatla Bharathi, IAS, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology, Government of Gujarat, in an exclusive interaction with Hemangini Kant Rajput and Elma Fatima of Elets News Network (ENN) , discusses the State’s priorities, the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2026–31, and the initiatives shaping Gujarat’s technology-led growth. As Secretary of the Department of Science & Technology, how do you view the Department’s role in driving Gujarat’s transition to a technology- and innovation-led economy? Science and technology today underpin industrial competitiveness, public-service delivery, healthcare, agriculture and sustainability, and the Department of Science & Technology is the nodal department steering this agenda for Gujarat. Our mandate is broad and deliberately integrated. It spans information technology and IT-enabled services, Global Capability Centres, semiconductors and electronics, biotechnology, space and emerging technologies, and the State’s digital-governance backbone. We deliver this mandate through a dedicated institutional framework. The Gujarat Council on Science and Technology (GUJCOST) anchors research promotion and the science ecosystem; the Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM), the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre and Gujarat Biotechnology University drive life-sciences research; Gujarat Science City advances science outreach; and the Directorate of ICT & e-Governance, together with Gujarat Informatics Limited, leads the State’s digital infrastructure and governance platforms. The Institute of Seismological Research (ISR) supports earthquake monitoring, seismic research and disaster resilience initiatives, while emerging initiatives such as NAMO Earth Science University are strengthening Gujarat’s Earth Sciences ecosystem. Our objective is to strengthen the entire innovation value chain, from research and talent development to technology commercialization and industry adoption, so that scientific capability translates into investment, jobs and competitiveness. The Department is significantly driving Gujarat’s transition towards AI-led governance, semiconductor manufacturing, digital public infrastructure, data centre ecosystem development and future technology adoption as key pillars of Viksit Gujarat. Q2. Gujarat recently unveiled the Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Policy 2026–31. What does it seek to achieve, and what are its principal pillars? The STI Policy 2026–31, announced in early 2026, is the framework that will guide the State’s science and innovation agenda over the next five years. Its ambition is to position Gujarat among the world’s leading innovation-driven economies by making research, technology and intellectual property central to industrial and societal development. bihar_raw_news.title: Ashutosh Gautam Takes Charge as NBCC Director (Projects) - eGov Magazine
bihar_raw_news.content: Home · e-Governance News NBCC (India) Limited , a Navratna public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs , has appointed Ashutosh Gautam as Director (Projects). Gautam assumed charge on Monday after approval by the competent authority, following an order issued by the ministry on October 19, 2026. Previously serving as Executive Director at Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) , Gautam will continue in the new position until his superannuation on April 30, 2029, or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Extensive Experience in Infrastructure Development Gautam brings more than 34 years of experience in infrastructure development, project execution and management. His professional work spans highways, ports, inland waterways and urban development, including major projects involving investments worth thousands of crores of rupees. Before joining RVNL, he served on deputation from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW). From February 2021 to May 2026, he served as Member (Technical) and Deputy Project Director of the Jal Marg Vikas Project (JMVP). During this period, he also held additional responsibilities as Member (Traffic and Logistics) at the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) and served as Member (Finance) for around seven months. Leadership Roles in Major Infrastructure Projects Gautam has held several leadership positions across infrastructure organisations. He served as Managing Director of Ahmedabad Vadodara Expressway Company Limited and as a Director on the board of Varanasi Multi-Modal Logistics Park Limited. Earlier, he worked as General Manager (Commercial Operations and Logistics) and as Project Director and nodal officer for World Bank-funded road projects. His responsibilities included work associated with the Golden Quadrilateral and the North-South and East-West Corridor programmes. He also spent around 12 years in Uttar Pradesh, coordinating World Bank-supported road projects across the state. Academic Qualifications and Professional Contributions Gautam holds a B.Tech in Civil Engineering and an M.Tech in Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi). His additional qualifications include an Advanced Management Programme in Infrastructure Development and Financing, a postgraduate diploma in Industrial Relations and Personnel Management, and an LLB in Corporate Law. Alongside his administrative responsibilities, Gautam has served as an honorary visiting faculty member at IITs, IIMs, the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA) and National Institutes of Technology. His teaching has focused on large-scale infrastructure projects, highway contract administration and FIDIC contracts. Contributions to Inland Waterways Development Gautam has also contributed to policy and institutional initiatives in the inland waterways sector. He represented IWAI and MoPSW in SGOS-2 during the preparation of Vision 2047 and served as Member Secretary for the development of the Inland Vessel Act and its associated rules under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. bihar_raw_news.content: ScanX News Ceigall India subsidiary secures financial close for ₹2,160 Cr highway project Ceigall India subsidiary secures financial close for ₹2,160 Cr highway project 2 min read | Published on 21 Oct 2026, 03:45 PM | Updated on 21 Oct 2026, 03:45 PM Reviewed by Jubin V ScanX News Team Add as a preferred source on Google Key Highlights Ceigall Sahebganj Bettiah Highway Limited secured financial close from NHAI on September 15, 2026 Project involves four-laning of 78.942 km of National Highway 139-W in Bihar Bid project cost stands at ₹2,160 crore under the Hybrid Annuity Mode Construction period is set at 730 days, followed by a 15-year O&M period powered by *this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only. Ceigall India announced that its subsidiary, Ceigall Sahebganj Bettiah Highway Limited, has received financial close approval from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for a major infrastructure project in Bihar. The intimation was filed with stock exchanges on October 21, 2026, confirming the completion of funding arrangements for the construction and operation of a key national highway. The project involves the four-laning of Sahebganj Areraj Bettiah on National Highway 139-W, spanning a total length of 78.942 km. The work is divided into two sections: Section 1 covers the stretch from Sahebganj to Areraj (38.362 km), while Section 2 covers the stretch from Areraj to Bettiah (40.580 km). The entire initiative is being executed under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM), a common structure for public-private partnership projects in India's road sector. Project specifics and timeline The bid project cost for this infrastructure development is fixed at ₹2,160 crore . The financial close date is recorded as September 15, 2026. Under the HAM model, the contractor is responsible for financing a portion of the project cost, with the government providing annuity payments over the concession period. This structure shifts significant execution risk to the developer while ensuring steady cash flows post-completion. The timeline for the project includes a 730-day construction period , followed by a 15-year operations and maintenance (O&M) period . This long-term O&M commitment ensures that the subsidiary will have a sustained revenue stream from maintenance contracts after the initial construction phase concludes. national_raw_news.content: In Punjab, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has taken over the investigation of Mansa-based anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota’s murder case. A team led by a senior Deputy Inspector General (DIG) level officer will examine the case with all the facts and figures. Earlier, the team of the investigative agency reached Mansa Police Station late last night to take over records. A new FIR has also been registered by the agency. Forensic experts, drug controllers and other experts are also reaching Mansa. According to sources, a post-mortem of the victim will be conducted by a team of doctors in PGI Chandigarh and an enquiry will be done by a Chandigarh-based Magistrate. Akashvani Jalandhar Correspondent reports that the action came within hours of the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah’s assurance of the CBI probe when he met Parvinder Singh’s family during his day-long visit to Punjab yesterday. Jhota was shot dead by a Chemist, Ashwani Kumar, last week, when he confronted the chemist for selling synthetic drugs. The Home Minister had also met another anti-drug activist, Vikramjit Singh’s family in Gurdaspur, who was also allegedly killed by drug traffickers for objecting to the sale of drugs. He also assured justice to the family of Gulzar Singh, who allegedly committed suicide in Sangrur recently, when his pleas were not heard by the state government against the sale of drugs, which made his son an addict.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games: India achieve spectacular podium sweep, clinching gold, silver, and bronze in m...
national_raw_news.content: India achieved a spectacular podium sweep at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Sachin Sarjerao Khilari, Mohd. Yasser, and Parveen clinched gold, silver, and bronze, respectively, in the men’s shot put F46 event today. Khilari led the Indian triumph with a record-breaking throw of 15.87 metres. Yasser secured the silver medal with a best throw of 15.06 metres, while Parveen claimed bronze with 14.94 metres. These athletes also recorded their Season Best performances, making it a memorable clean sweep for India on the podium. India’s Praveen Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump T44/64 with a Games record, while Banti clinched silver in the same event in Aichi Nagoya, Japan today. Praveen sailed over 2.05m to win the gold while Banti produced a personal best of 1.92m to take the silver. Temurbek Giyazov of Uzbekistan was third with 1.86m. Ayush Verma also won gold medal in the men’s shot put F53 event today, adding a second medal to his tally. Ayush produced a throw of 8.16m in his fifth attempt to take the top spot. Alireza Hemami of Iran was second with 8.09m while Makhambet Serikkaliyev of Kazakhstan finished third with 6.81m. F53 is for field athletes who have movement affected to a high degree in the trunk and legs and hand grip affected to a low level. Teenage Indian pair of para-archers Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag clinched a silver medal after losing in the compound women’s doubles final today. Sheetal, who was born without arms, and Payal, a quadruple amputee, went down 141-150 to the Chinese duo of Xu Xueqing and Zhao Jing. Sheetal had won a silver medal in this event in the last edition of the Games partnering Sarita Devi. In the men’s 100m T35 event Anubhav Choudhary secured Bronze medal. He clocked a personal best of 12.72 seconds to win the medal. Rakeshbhai Bhatt also won bronze medal in men’s 100 meter T37 event.

national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah calls upon police forces to work towards eliminating drug menace by end o...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today said that the government has set a target to eliminate the drug menace from India by 31st December, 2029. Speaking at the Police Commemoration Day ceremony at the National Police Memorial in New Delhi, Mr Shah called upon police forces across the country to work towards eliminating narcotics by the end of 2029. He said, the drug menace is a serious challenge as it damages future generations, places an undue burden on the economy and provides financial support to organisations involved in anti-national activities. The Home Minister said that the country has liberated itself from the menace of Naxalism on the 31st of March this year. Paying tributes to police personnel who laid down their lives in the service of the nation, Mr Shah said that the country had endured the pain of Naxalism from 1981 until March 2026. During this period, more than three thousand six hundred security personnel and nearly 13 thousand innocent civilians lost their lives. Home Minister Shah said a total of 36 thousand 852 police personnel have laid down their lives in the line of duty since Independence. He said the country’s citizens remained grateful for the sacrifices made by the martyrs and their families. Mr Shah said that the sacrifices of Police Personnel had laid the foundation for the country’s progress and development. The Minister said that the nation could not have safeguarded its internal and external security without the supreme sacrifices made by police personnel. The Minister said that the protection of the country’s democracy and the smooth functioning of the democratic system are not possible without Central Armed Police Forces. He said, electoral violence has ended in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Mr Shah said, this time, due to the vigilance of the security forces, elections in West Bengal were conducted without any violence for the first time. Earlier, Union Home Minister flagged off a nationwide motorcycle rally from the National Police Memorial to mark the National Police Commemoration Day. The bike rally, organised under the theme Fight Against Drugs, comprises around 90 riders representing nine States and Union Territories, alongside personnel from Central Armed Police Forces and Central Police Organisations.

national_raw_news.title: 2 killed, 17 injured as passenger bus plunges into deep gorge in Udhampur, J&K 22 mins ago 12
national_raw_news.content: In Jammu and Kashmir, two people, including a five-year-old child and a 25-year-old woman, lost their lives, while 17 others were injured after a passenger bus skidded off the road and plunged into a deep gorge at Gulli Gala in the Pachiound area of Basantgarh tehsil in Udhampur district today. Akashvani correspondent reports that the bus was travelling from Pachiound towards Ramnagar when the accident occurred. A total of 19 people initially sustained injuries, of whom two subsequently succumbed during treatment, leaving 17 injured survivors. Local residents were among the first to reach the accident site and launched rescue operations to evacuate passengers trapped inside the damaged vehicle. Personnel from Majodi Police Post subsequently joined the rescue efforts. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed grief over the loss of lives in the tragic accident and conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah also expressed deep sorrow over the incident and directed the authorities to ensure the best possible medical care and assistance to the injured. The Chief Minister’s Office is in constant touch with the concerned authorities and closely monitoring the situation. Meanwhile, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh spoke to Deputy Commissioner Udhampur Ananth Dwivedi after receiving news of the accident to review the situation and ongoing relief measures. He said all passengers were promptly evacuated following the timely intervention of local residents and assured that all necessary assistance was being provided. Police have registered a case and initiated an investigation to ascertain the exact cause of the accident. Further details are awaited.

national_raw_news.title: DRI seizes more than 9 kg of methamphetamine in intensified crackdown on synthetic drug ...
national_raw_news.content: DRI seizes more than 9 kg of methamphetamine in intensified crackdown on synthetic drug trafficking in Bhopal; One held Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर DRI seizes more than 9 kg of methamphetamine in intensified crackdown on synthetic drug trafficking in Bhopal; One held ANI | Updated: Oct 21, 2026 19:52 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 21 (ANI): In a significant crackdown on synthetic drug trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence ( DRI ) has seized 9.139 kg of methamphetamine and arrested one person at the Inter-State Bus Terminal (ISBT), Bhopal , on October 20. According to the Ministry of Finance , the seizure highlights DRI ’s sustained efforts to disrupt the movement of dangerous synthetic drugs through the country’s inter-city transport networks. Acting on specific intelligence, officers of DRI intercepted an Indian male passenger travelling by bus from Delhi to Bengaluru upon the bus’s arrival at Bhopal ISBT. Examination of the passenger’s baggage led to the recovery of 11 plastic packets containing crystalline methamphetamine, weighing 9.139 kg, concealed inside packets of salwar suits and carried in two mid-sized trolley bags. Field testing confirmed the presence of methamphetamine in the recovered substance, which was seized and the passenger was arrested under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. This seizure comes amid growing concerns over the trafficking of synthetic drugs in the country. In recent major operations, DRI seized 231.8 kg of Meth tablets in the North-Eastern region, suspected to have been smuggled from Myanmar and 137 kg of suspected crystal methamphetamine in Tamil Nadu, where the consignment was allegedly intended for onward smuggling to Sri Lanka through a maritime route. These operations underscore the scale and varied routes of synthetic drug trafficking, spanning inter-city transport networks, cross-border and coastal corridors. Through sustained intelligence-led enforcement, DRI remains committed to dismantling narcotics trafficking networks and preventing dangerous drugs from reaching illicit markets. national_raw_news.title: World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency
national_raw_news.content: World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency - India Today India Today Aaj Tak India Today Hindi NewsTak GNTTV Lallantop Business Today Bangla Malayalam Northeast BT Bazaar Harper's Bazaar Sports Tak Astro Tak Gaming Brides Today Cosmopolitan Kisan Tak Reader’s Digest India Today Aaj Tak India Today Hindi NewsTak GNTTV Lallantop Business Today Bangla Malayalam Northeast SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News Health World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency Iodine plays a vital role in thyroid hormone production, metabolism and brain development. Adequate iodine intake, particularly during pregnancy and childhood, can help prevent serious health complications. Advertisement World Iodine Deficiency Day 2026: How iodised salt helps prevent health problems By: India Today Health Desk New Delhi , Oct 21, 2026 11:19 IST Last Updated Oct 21, 2026 11:19 IST Published by Smarica Pant Oct 21, 2026 11:17 IST Iodine is an essential mineral that the body needs to produce thyroid hormones, which regulate metabolism, growth and development. Although the body needs only small amounts of iodine, insufficient intake can lead to several health problems, including thyroid disorders and impaired brain development. The risks are especially serious during pregnancy and early childhood, when the brain and nervous system develop rapidly. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story World Iodine Deficiency Day, also known as Global Iodine Deficiency Disorders Prevention Day, is observed on October 21 every year to raise awareness about the importance of iodine and the consequences of its deficiency. In India, the government has introduced several initiatives to promote iodised salt consumption and reduce iodine deficiency disorders. Here is what you need to know about iodine, its health benefits and the steps being taken to prevent deficiency. WHAT IS IODINE AND WHY DOES THE BODY NEED IT Iodine is a mineral required to produce the thyroid hormone's thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). These hormones help regulate metabolism, body temperature, growth and energy use. Iodine is naturally present in certain foods, including seafood, dairy products and eggs. Iodised salt is another important source. The amount of iodine in food depends on factors such as soil conditions and food production methods. World Iodine Deficiency day (Picture credit: pib.gov.in) HEALTH RISKS OF IODINE DEFICIENCY Insufficient iodine intake can prevent the thyroid gland from producing enough hormones. This may lead to hypothyroidism, which can cause tiredness, weight gain and other symptoms. Goitre, or an enlarged thyroid gland, is another possible sign of iodine deficiency. During pregnancy, severe iodine deficiency can affect fetal growth and brain development and increase the risk of miscarriage and stillbirth. In infants and children, inadequate iodine can affect cognitive development and learning. Prolonged deficiency can also affect growth and overall health. INDIA'S EFFORTS TO PREVENT IODINE DEFICIENCY India launched the National Goitre Control Programme in 1962 to address iodine deficiency. In 1992, it was expanded and renamed the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme...

national_raw_news.title: SBI data breach: PSU bank confirms 3,897 customer records exposed on dark web
national_raw_news.content: SBI data breach: PSU bank confirms 3,897 customer records exposed on dark web - Telangana Today NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Business | Sbi Data Breach Psu Bank Confirms 3897 Customer Records Exposed On Dark Web SBI data breach: PSU bank confirms 3,897 customer records exposed on dark web State Bank of India confirmed that 3,897 customer records containing personal information were identified during a preliminary analysis of data found on the dark web. The lender has launched an investigation and said the incident has not disrupted core business operations By IANS Published Date - 21 October 2026, 10:43 AM New Delhi: State Bank of India (SBI) — India’s largest lender — on Wednesday clarified that it experienced a data breach with 3,897 customer records found exposed on the dark web. According to the bank, it has received communications from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In regarding an alert concerning suspected exposure of customer data earlier in the week. During preliminary analysis of approximately 375,000 records available on the dark web, 3,897 customer records containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) were identified, the bank said in an exchange filing. The exposed information reportedly included customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files, it added. The state-owned bank further noted that it promptly activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent CERT-In-empanelled cybersecurity agency to conduct a comprehensive assessment and investigate the nature and extent of the alleged compromise. The bank said a detailed investigation is underway to establish authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine potential source and extent of exposure and assess associated risks. The incident does not have any material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity and core functions continue to operate normally without disruption, the bank said adding that appropriate remedial and preventive measures are being implemented. Shares of SBI on Wednesday traded on a flat note at Rs 970 at around 10 am on the BSE. The banking stock recorded a 52-week high of Rs 1,234.80 and a 52-week low of Rs 891.55, according to the exchange data. In the last one-year horizon, it declined 12 per cent but gained over the last five years. Earlier in the week, an unidentified hacker group operating under the name ‘Siriusim’ claimed to have obtained confidential customer information allegedly linked to the State Bank of India (SBI), including personal details, loan applications and account-opening documents. The claim was highlighted by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse56 in a post on social media platform X. The group purportedly possesses 3.75 lakh data entries in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents associated with the country’s largest public sector lender, as per the post. national_raw_news.content: 'No Double Standards On Terrorism': At SCO Summit, Rajnath Singh Calls For Collective Action To Dismantle Terror Ecosystem Security 'No Double Standards On Terrorism': At SCO Summit, Rajnath Singh Calls For Collective Action To Dismantle Terror Ecosystem Swarajya Staff Oct 21, 2026 | Updated 08:53 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Defence Minister Rajnath Singh (Pic Via PIB) Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday (20 October) called upon Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states to work together to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, asserting that there could be no justification for the menace or double standards in dealing with it. Addressing the 25th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on Tuesday, Singh described terrorism as one of the gravest threats to peace, development and economic prosperity. Singh said terrorism undermines not only human lives but also economic activity and social development, disrupting investment and commerce whilst depriving young people of opportunities. The Defence Minister emphasised that there can be no justification for terrorism, stating that there should be no double standards in dealing with the threat and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. His remarks came in the presence of Pakistan Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar at the regional summit. The minister stressed that the entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively dismantled by member states. Singh also recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi's emphasis at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August-September 2026 on taking concrete steps in security, connectivity and economic cooperation. He said terrorism not only claims innocent lives but also radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. While addressing connectivity and economic cooperation, Singh emphasised that connectivity projects must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries. He stressed that projects not founded on these principles would not be sustainable, calling for simplified customs procedures, digital documentation, improved logistics and interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business amongst SCO member states.
